arxiv-2109-10102.creator: Uyen Tu Lieu, Natsuhiko Yoshinaga
arxiv-2109-10102.description: Abstract We propose an optimisation method for the inverse structural design of self-assembly of anisotropic patchy particles. The anisotropic interaction can be expressed by the spherical harmonics of the surface pattern on a patchy particle, and thus arbitrary symmetry of the patch can be treated.

arxiv-2408-05867.title: SABER-6D: Shape Representation Based Implicit Object Pose Estimation
arxiv-2408-05867.creator: Shishir Reddy Vutukur, Mengkejiergeli Ba, Benjamin Busam, Matthias Kayser, Gurprit Singh
arxiv-2408-05867.description: Abstract In this paper, we propose a novel encoder-decoder architecture, named SABER, to learn the 6D pose of the object in the embedding space by learning shape representation at a given pose. This model enables us to learn pose by performing shape representation at a target pose from RGB image input.

arxiv-2411-03333.title: Analysis of Bipartite Networks in Anime Series: Textual Analysis, Topic Clustering, and Modeling
arxiv-2411-03333.creator: Juan Sosa, Alejandro Urrego-Lopez, Cesar Prieto
arxiv-2411-03333.description: Abstract This article analyzes a specific bipartite network that shows the relationships between users and anime, examining how the descriptions of anime influence the formation of user communities. In particular, we introduce a new variable that quantifies the frequency with which words from a description appear in specific word clusters.

arxiv-2503-01506.title: SampleMix: A Sample-wise Pre-training Data Mixing Strategey by Coordinating Data Quality and Diversity
arxiv-2503-01506.creator: Xiangyu Xi, Deyang Kong, Jian Yang, JiaWei Yang, Zhengyu Chen, Wei Wang, Jingang Wang, Xunliang Cai, Shikun Zhang, Wei Ye
arxiv-2503-01506.description: Abstract Existing pretraining data mixing methods for large language models (LLMs) typically follow a domain-wise methodology, a top-down process that first determines domain weights and then performs uniform data sampling across each domain. However, these approaches neglect significant inter-domain overlaps and commonalities, failing to control the global diversity of the constructed training dataset.

arxiv-2506-09701.title: TRIDENT: Temporally Restricted Inference via DFA-Enhanced Neural Traversal
arxiv-2506-09701.creator: Vincenzo Collura, Karim Tit, Laura Bussi, Eleonora Giunchiglia, Maxime Cordy
arxiv-2506-09701.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) and other neural architectures have achieved impressive results across a variety of generative and classification tasks. However, they remain fundamentally ill-equipped to ensure that their outputs satisfy temporal constraints, such as those expressible in Linear Temporal Logic over finite traces ( LTL f \text{LTL}_{f} ).

arxiv-2506-10215.title: Isoholonomic inequalities and speed limits for cyclic quantum systems
arxiv-2506-10215.creator: Ole Sönnerborn
arxiv-2506-10215.description: Abstract Quantum speed limits set fundamental lower bounds on the time required for a quantum system to evolve between states. Traditional bounds—such as those by Mandelstam-Tamm and Margolus-Levitin—rely on state distinguishability and become trivial for cyclic evolutions where the initial and final states coincide.

pmc-12392514.title: The impact of clinical simulation on bridging the theory–practice gap in nursing education: a systematic review
pmc-12392514.creator: Majid Daneshfar, Hossein Karimi Moonaghi
pmc-12392514.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundBridging the gap between theoretical instruction and practical competence remains a central challenge in nursing education. Nursing students often struggle to transfer classroom-acquired knowledge into real-world clinical environments, resulting in decreased confidence, impaired decision-making, and compromised patient care. Clinical simulation has emerged as a promising pedagogical tool to address this longstanding theory–practice gap by recreating realistic scenarios in a controlled setting.MethodThis systematic review synthesized studies published from 2010 to 2025 concerning the use of clinical simulation in nursing education.

pmc-12771823.title: Dual block evidence of the effects of topiramate, a sulfamate-substituted monosaccharide, on voltage-gated sodium current and hyperpolarization-activated cation current
pmc-12771823.creator: Ray-Chang Tzeng, Ming-Chi Lai, Sheng-Nan Wu, Chin-Wei Huang
pmc-12771823.description: BackgroundTopiramate (TPM) is a sulfamate-substituted monosaccharide known for its wide-ranging effects on epilepsy, neuropathic pain, and migraines. However, its precise influence on plasmalemmal ionic currents, including their magnitude and gating kinetics, remains uncertain. Therefore, a reassessment of the regulatory effect of TPM on ionic currents in electrically excitable cells is warranted.

uslaw-usc-t5-s7324.title: 5 U.S.C. § 7324 — Political activities on duty; prohibition
uslaw-usc-t5-s7324.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t5-s7324.description: United States Code, Title 5 (Government Organization And Employees); Part III (Employees); Subpart F (Labor-Management And Employee Relations); Chapter 73 (Suitability, Security, And Conduct); Subchapter III (Political Activities). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) An employee may not engage in political activity— (1) while the employee is on duty; (2) in any room or building occupied in the discharge of official duties.
